body:
Two independent gaps in `cps/api/edit.py:set_cover`:

1. No `helper.book_cover_is_locked` check. `cover_picker.cover_picker_apply` refuses every
   apply kind with a 409 while the per-book cover lock is set (janeczku/calibre-web#2165), and
   the classic editor honours it on its cover-URL path. The SPA endpoint writes regardless, so a
   user who deliberately locked a cover can have it replaced from the new UI's edit page.
2. It resolves the book with `calibre_db.get_filtered_book(book_id)` using strict defaults,
   while `cps/api/books.py`'s detail endpoint deliberately passes
   `allow_show_archived=True, allow_show_hidden=True` so a user can open their OWN hidden or
   archived book. The neighbouring delete endpoints in the same module pass those flags too.
   Result: the edit page opens, and replacing the cover 404s.

Found by an adversarial review of PR #1739. Not fixed there: both are behaviour changes
unrelated to that PR's cache policy, and (1) in particular would newly refuse writes that
currently succeed, which deserves its own change and its own release note.
title: SPA cover endpoint ignores the cover lock and 404s on the user's own hidden or archived book
